borrow_or_financing: none (long-only IWM/IJR/IWC/VB/SPY/QQQ/SHY, no leverage, no shorting)
cost_model: sum(abs(delta_weight)) * slippage_bps, charged on the execution session (next session open after the close signal)
k2_control_cost_model: the vol-matched k*S3+(1-k)*SHY control pays no rebalancing cost (conservative in the control's favor, matching every prior batch-screening round's convention)
note_vs_source: Ko & Yang (2021) is an index-level academic study with no cost model or tradable-ETF fill assumption at all -- this project's frozen contract (close-signal -> next-session-open fill, 10bp/20bp per side) is applied unedited, identical to every other screen_lane batch. Given the low trade frequency (~9-10 entries/year per candidate), the cost drag is small in absolute terms but so is the expected gross premium (Ko & Yang's own 1983-2019 magnitude is 0.14-0.37pp per single pre-holiday session), so cost sensitivity is reported explicitly (10bp vs 20bp CAGR) in report.md rather than assumed negligible.
